title.narrative: ROAP/AFG07/23/Data Collection Survey on Community Infrastructure Recovery in Earthquake Affected Areas in Herat Province: Building resilient community infrastructure in Afghanistan through a build-back-better approach

description.narrative: In October 2023, 4 powerful (6.3 magnitude) earthquakes struck Herat Province, western Afghanistan resulting in wide-scale destruction across more than 300 villages with nearly 43,400 people reported to be directly affected. In addition to loss of life and injury, the earthquakes destroyed critical civilian infrastructure, including homes, health facilities, and water networks. At least 21 health facilities across 9 districts were damaged, resulting in severe disruptions in access to health services for an estimated 580,000 people (OCHA, 2023). At least 7,023 houses have been affected across 7 districts with 47% destroyed and 30% severely damaged (Shelter Cluster, 2023). It has been reported that Zindajan District has been devastated the most in the province by the earthqukes. The project’s objective is to support the development of resilient community infrastructure in the earthquake-affected areas in Zindajan District, Herat Province, Afghanistan by taking a building back better (BBB) approach. Based on the spatial plans to be developed, UN-Habitat will rehabilitate and retrofit the selected public health facility in Herat with the provision of essential medical equipment and solar power system. This activity will include the improvement of WASH system inside and around the selected health facility (e.g., drinking water systems, paved road and roadside drainages, toilets, waste management systems and sewer canals) as an integral part of resilient community infrastructure.
